home.headline: Stablecoins rarely beat the cheapest transfer app. But where banks won't sell you dollars, they're how people get one.
home.headlineFallback: Stablecoins rarely beat the cheapest transfer app. But where banks won't sell you dollars, they're how people get one.
home.headlineSub: Four AI agents run this site every hour. They track what a dollar costs on the street in 60 countries, and what it costs to send money with an app or with stablecoins. How it was built →
home.purposeNote: Built to test one claim: that stablecoins make moving money cheaper.
home.allCountriesTitle: What a dollar costs on the street vs the official rate, every country we track
home.allCountriesNote: Where the gap is near zero, the official rate is real and a normal app is cheaper. Where the gap is big, the official rate isn't what people pay, and stablecoins are how people get dollars at all.
home.allCountriesPeggedLegend: Light grey: pegged currency, the gap is the cost of buying stablecoins.

hero.title: What does a dollar really cost?
hero.body: In much of the world the official exchange rate is not the rate anyone gets. This measures what people actually pay for a dollar — the kind an ordinary person can buy on their phone — in {count} currencies, every hour. Where there is no price, it says so, and why.

market.hint: Click any country on the board to see its history here. Hover the chart to read a point, click to pin it.

board.title: What a dollar really costs
board.subhead: measured every hour · furthest above the official rate first
board.withheldNote: A price was collected for these and stored, but it does not meet the evidence rule, so it is not shown as a number. Each country keeps its page and its reason, and returns as soon as its market does.
board.footnote: Each row is one country. "A dollar costs" is what you pay to buy one dollar there, against the official exchange rate captured in the same second. "Round trip" is what it costs to buy and then sell again. Click any country for every source behind its number.
board.gapsNote: The eight countries where a dollar costs the most above the official rate.
board.pricedNote: Each one links to its own page, with the full history and the receipt behind the number.

cross.title: If you moved money through stablecoins, what rate would you get?
cross.intro: Turn {baseCode} into a digital dollar on a {baseCountry} exchange, then turn that dollar into the other country's money on an exchange there. This is the rate that round trip works out to, next to the official rate for the same moment.
cross.footnote: A plus means the dollar route works out to more of the other country's money than the official rate would give you, before any fees.
cross.empty: No pair has both currencies priced in the same hour yet.

coverage.title: Is the data complete?
coverage.footnote: Prices from before August 2026 are daily, not hourly, so they appear in the history chart but never in this grid.

correction.label: Correction on the record
correction.title: I published a wrong number once
correction.body: My first version said the dollar route beat Wise by 3x. Then I checked the exchanges' real fees, and it didn't. {makerProse}. The mistake stays on the page so you can see the numbers here get checked, including mine.

footer.body: Built by Sebastian Roervig. I work in cross-border payments. Everyone says stablecoins made moving money cheap. I couldn't find anyone who had measured it, so I did. Raw data and code: github.com/SebR214/margin

ask.note: Answered from files already in this repo — nothing is fetched over the network and nothing is guessed. Free-form questions arrive once the question-answering key is switched on; until then, these are the questions it can answer.

Which country is closest to the official rate right now?

receipt.evidenceOffersNote: Every offer collected that hour is listed below.

receipt.rateManaged: A rate the government sets and defends.
receipt.ratePegged: A rate this currency is pegged to.
receipt.rateUnmaintained: A rate that has stopped being updated — this compares against an average of what banks quote instead.
receipt.rateStalenessNote: This value is refreshed every hour but the underlying source itself only changes about once a day, so it can be up to 24 hours behind the market.
receipt.verdictPublished: Published — the evidence rule was met.
receipt.verdictNoteOrderBook: The minimum-offer rule applies to peer-to-peer sources only. This price comes from an order book or a broker quote instead, evidenced by how many exchanges quoted it.
receipt.verdictNoteAggregate: A single aggregated price from an independent source, not a two-sided listing board — there is no offer count to test.
receipt.loadErrorTemplate: The receipt at {file} could not be read.

machineRoom.title: The machine room
machineRoom.lede: Four programs do the work here. One checks prices every hour. One builds the site. One checks what got built. One decides what to build next. This page shows them working, live, with nothing cleaned up first.
